🔥🇲🇽 <u>Mexico's New Judicial Disciplinary Court Sends Six Federal Judges to the Prosecutor</u>

The Judicial Disciplinary Court (TDJ), created by the 2024 judicial reform, asked the Attorney General's Office (FGR) to investigate six suspended federal judges for possible crimes, including unlawful exercise of public office. One case involves a court administrator in Mexico City who changed a colleague's bank routing number and pocketed their paycheck. In its first year, the TDJ has opened 248 cases against judicial officials. For decades, nobody policed Mexico's judges except the judges themselves.
banner: DISCIPLINE COURT SENDS 6 JUDGES TO FGR

🇲🇽🏛️ <u>Mexico Has Closed 37 Prisons Since 2018, Including Islas Marías</u>

From December 2018 to August 2026, Mexico shut down 37 prisons: 32 run by state governments, five federal maximum-security facilities, and the Islas Marías penal colony, which AMLO turned into an environmental and cultural center. The prison population rose over the same period from 200,936 to 275,554, and 158 facilities are now overcrowded, according to reports from the federal prison agency (OAPRS). That is the gap the six new federal prisons announced this month, with no private operators, are meant to close.

🇲🇽✊ "It's like a revolution, only it's digital. It is a digital transformation for the benefit of the people." — Presidenta Claudia Sheinbaum, Ciudad del Carmen, Campeche On a Quintana Roo hospital visit she was told a special type of glove was missing. Birmex said they had been bought; they were sitting in the state's medical-supply warehouse. Hospital directors still request supplies by official letter, sometimes carried by hand for hours across the state, time they can't spend on patients. She said she will present a plan at a mañanera to digitize and automate the warehouses. Instead of hiring a company, she will convene young Mexican data-science and logistics graduates from TecNM, IPN, UNAM and Campeche's university: if shoes ordered from China arrive the next day, "how can we not get the gloves from the warehouse to the hospital?"
banner: GLOVES IN STOCK, NOT IN HOSPITALS

text: 🔥🇲🇽 "27,000 beds in the first 39 years, and 4,000 in the following 36 years." — Presidenta Claudia Sheinbaum, Ciudad del Carmen, Campeche She named the six neoliberal presidents (De la Madrid, Salinas, Zedillo, Fox, Calderón, Peña Nieto) and said those 36 years built the idea that public is bad and had to be privatized. From its founding in 1943 to 1982, IMSS built hospitals totaling 27,000 beds; in the next 36 years, 4,000. Meanwhile the minimum wage stagnated, contributions shrank, enrollment grew, and junk food drove up diabetes and hypertension. Specialty exam slots for young doctors were cut. Now, she said, twice as many are accepted into specialties, and every graduate is hired by ISSSTE, IMSS or IMSS-Bienestar.

🔥🇲🇽 "Some even own TV stations. They used to have health contracts and now they don't, so they devote the TV station to going after us, many times with falsehoods. Why? Because they can no longer sell services or medicines." — Presidenta Claudia Sheinbaum, Ciudad del Carmen, Campeche She said that under neoliberalism, care for people without social security was handed to each state's own system. States with few residents and many needs, like Campeche, couldn't cover it, and contracting was riddled with corruption. López Obrador merged those systems into IMSS-Bienestar, now in 24 states, so doctors and equipment can be shared. Consolidated purchasing is cutting drug prices: "Medicines are very expensive, and it's a handful of pharmaceutical companies that sell them."
banner: LOST HEALTH CONTRACTS, NOW TV ATTACKS

text: 🇲🇽🎨 "If education is paid for, it becomes a commodity, it becomes a privilege." — Presidenta Claudia Sheinbaum, Ciudad del Carmen, Campeche She told how she met ISSSTE director Martí Batres 40 years ago in a UNAM student movement. She studied physics at the Faculty of Sciences; he was at Preparatoria 7. The rector said students had to pay or they wouldn't value their education. Students answered in a public dialogue (10 authorities against 10 students) that education is a right under Article 3 of the 1917 Constitution. They marched, always peacefully, and won: the rector had to back down. Other universities did impose fees. Today her government is opening more free public universities, including the Rosario Castellanos National University.

🇲🇽✊ "The best health system for those who have the least." — Presidenta Claudia Sheinbaum, Ciudad del Carmen, Campeche She recalled building Mexico City's Cablebús from the humblest part of Iztapalapa on the principle of "the best transport for those who have the least," and said health must work the same way: "Translated another way: for the good of all, first the poor." A president, she said, could isolate herself in the National Palace and only receive businessmen. Instead she spends weekends at IMSS-Bienestar hospitals (Hidalgo, State of Mexico, Quintana Roo, Yucatán, now Campeche), talking with doctors, nurses and patients. "The way of governing is different: walking, listening and transforming."

🇲🇽✊ "We firmly believe that public must be synonymous with excellence." — Alejandro Svarch Pérez, director general of IMSS-Bienestar, Ciudad del Carmen, Campeche On October 18 the president handed over the full rehabilitation of the Dra. María del Socorro Quiroga Aguilar General Hospital in Ciudad del Carmen, open for 35 years. Svarch said 100% of the facilities were renewed while it kept operating; ISSSTE, the naval hospital, Pemex and IMSS lent their operating rooms during the works. Beds went from 62 to 94. Pediatrics, emergency and intensive care capacity doubled, and a pediatric emergency area was created for the first time. The state's most advanced CT scanner (128-slice) was installed. Cardiology, nephrology, neurology and pediatric neurology are offered there for the first time. Care is 100% free.

🇲🇽🌧️ <u>S&P: El Niño Puts 10 Mexican State Economies on the Line</u>

According to S&P National Ratings, cited by El Economista, more than 34% of state GDP in Baja California Sur, Durango, Jalisco, Morelos, Nayarit, Quintana Roo, Sinaloa, Tlaxcala, Veracruz and Yucatán comes from climate-sensitive tourism, farming and food industries. Nationally those sectors hold about 24% of local jobs, a share that averages 39% in Baja California Sur, Quintana Roo and Nayarit. The agency rates the national impact as moderate compared with other emerging markets. The squeeze lands on state budgets, which face slower growth and higher emergency spending at the same time.
banner: EL NIÑO: 10 STATES >34% OF GDP EXPOSED

🔥🇲🇽 <u>Mexico's Right Still Celebrates the Conquest</u>

Since AMLO's December 2020 decree, Mexico has marked October 12 as the Day of the Pluricultural Nation instead of "Día de la Raza." The right hasn't let go. PAN Mexico City lawmaker América Rangel posts tributes to Hispanidad and to the fall of the Mexica empire. In May, Cuauhtémoc mayor Alessandra Rojo de la Vega received Madrid's Isabel Díaz Ayuso at her offices. On that same tour, at an event titled "Celebration of Evangelization and Mestizaje in Mexico," Ayuso declared: "Without Cortés, there would be no Mexico."
